extracted.intended_audience: national patent offices, patent attorneys/agents, Contracting States' government delegates and officials involved in PCT administration
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedural rules, and administrative requirements under the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) and its Regulations governing rights to practice, information and technical assistance, governance, finances, amendment procedures, entry into force, reservations, and the formal requirements for international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to practice before international authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attorney, patent agent, or other person, having the right to practice before the national Office with which the international application was filed, shall be entitled to practice before the International Bureau and the competent International Searching Authority and competent International Preliminary Examining Authority in respect of that application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants practicing rights before IB, ISA and IPEA to persons already entitled to practice before the receiving national Office for that application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of patent information services
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau may provide information services, directly or through one or more International Searching Authorities or other national or international specialized institutions, with which the International Bureau may reach agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Services may be operated directly by the IB or outsourced/arranged with ISAs or specialized institutions by agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operation of information services to facilitate developing countries
rubrics_metrics.description: The information services shall be operated in a way particularly facilitating the acquisition by Contracting States which are developing countries of technical knowledge and technology, including available published know-how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit objective that services be tailored to improve access for developing countries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of information services
rubrics_metrics.description: The information services shall be available to Governments of Contracting States and their nationals and residents. The Assembly may decide to make these services available also to others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary beneficiaries are Contracting States' governments and their nationals/residents; Assembly may expand access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pricing policy for services to governments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any service to Governments of Contracting States shall be furnished at cost, provided that, when the Government is that of a Contracting State which is a developing country, the service shall be furnished below cost if the difference can be covered from profit made on services furnished to others than Governments of Contracting States or from the sources referred to in Article 51(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost is understood as 'cost over and above costs normally incident to the performance of the services of a national Office or the obligations of an International Searching Authority.' Implementation details governed by Assembly decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly governance of implementation and financing
rubrics_metrics.description: The details concerning the implementation of the provisions of this Article shall be governed by decisions of the Assembly and, within the limits to be fixed by the Assembly, such working groups as the Assembly may set up for that purpose. The Assembly shall, when it considers it necessary, recommend methods of providing financing supplementary to those referred to in paragraph (5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly sets implementation details, can establish working groups, and may recommend supplementary financing methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau technical assistance (information services)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau may furnish services by providing technical and any other pertinent information available to it on the basis of published documents, primarily patents and published applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB's technical assistance is based on published patent literature and related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee for Technical Assistance — establishment and membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall establish a Committee for Technical Assistance. The members of the Committee shall be elected among the Contracting States, with due regard to the representation of developing countries. The Director General shall, on his own initiative or at the request of the Committee, invite representatives of intergovernmental organizations concerned with technical assistance to developing countries to participate in the work of the Committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee composition must consider developing country representation; DG may invite intergovernmental organizations as participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of technical assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The task of the Committee shall be to organize and supervise technical assistance for Contracting States which are developing countries in developing their patent systems individually or on a regional basis. The technical assistance shall comprise, among other things, the training of specialists, the loaning of experts, and the supply of equipment both for demonstration and for operational purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assistance covers capacity-building, expert loans, and equipment for demonstration and operations; IB shall seek financing agreements with international financing organizations and governments of recipient States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-affect of other financial treaty provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Chapter shall affect the financial provisions contained in any other Chapter of this Treaty. Such provisions are not applicable to the present Chapter or to its implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial rules elsewhere in the Treaty remain unaffected; separates Chapter IV provisions from other financial provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly composition and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall consist of the Contracting States. The Government of each Contracting State shall be represented by one delegate, who may be assisted by alternate delegates, advisors, and experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every Contracting State is a member and has one vote (see voting rule), with delegation allowed to be assisted by alternates/advisors/experts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly functions and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall deal with all matters concerning the maintenance and development of the Union and the implementation of this Treaty; perform tasks specifically assigned under other provisions; give directions to the International Bureau concerning preparation for revision conferences; review and approve reports and activities of the Director General and Executive Committee; determine program and adopt triennial budget; adopt financial regulations; establish committees and working groups; determine observer admission; and take any other appropriate action to further the objectives of the Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly has broad oversight, budgetary, regulatory and organizational powers as listed in Article 53(2)(a)(i)-(x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assembly voting, quorum and decision thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Contracting State shall have one vote. One-half of the Contracting States shall constitute a quorum. In the absence of the quorum, the Assembly may make decisions but (except for procedural decisions) such decisions shall take effect only if the quorum and the required majority are attained through voting by correspondence as provided in the Regulations. Subject to certain provisions, decisions of the Assembly shall require two-thirds of the votes cast. Abstentions shall not be considered as votes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quorum = one-half of Contracting States; decisions normally require two-thirds of votes cast; abstentions are not votes; special applicability rules apply where only some States are bound by parts of the Treaty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of Executive Committee when membership exceeds forty
rubrics_metrics.description: When the number of Contracting States exceeds forty, the Assembly shall establish an Executive Committee. Any reference to the Executive Committee in this Treaty and the Regulations shall be construed as references to such Committee once it has been established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triggers creation of Executive Committee and thereafter references apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee composition, election and term limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall consist of States elected by the Assembly from among States members of the Assembly. The number of States members of the Executive Committee shall correspond to one-fourth of the number of States members of the Assembly (remainders disregarded). In electing members, the Assembly shall have due regard to an equitable geographical distribution. Each member shall serve from the close of the session of the Assembly which elected it to the close of the next ordinary session; members may be re-elected but only up to a maximum of two-thirds of such members. The Assembly shall establish rules governing election and possible re-election.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Committee seats are proportional (1/4) with geographic balance and limits on re-election; Assembly defines details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall: prepare the draft agenda of the Assembly; submit proposals to the Assembly in respect of the draft program and biennial budget of the Union prepared by the Director General; submit, with appropriate comments, to the Assembly the periodical reports of the Director General and the yearly audit reports on the accounts; take all necessary measures to ensure the execution of the program of the Union by the Director General, in accordance with the decisions of the Assembly; and perform such other functions as are allocated to it under this Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Executive Committee acts as preparatory and supervisory body for Assembly business and execution of programs between sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Committee meeting and voting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Executive Committee shall meet once a year in ordinary session and in extraordinary session upon convocation. Each State member shall have one vote. One-half of the members constitute a quorum. Decisions shall be made by a simple majority of the votes cast. Abstentions shall not be considered as votes. A delegate may represent, and vote in the name of, one State only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary meetings annually; simple majority decision rule; usual quorum/abstention rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau roles and Director General responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative tasks concerning the Union shall be performed by the International Bureau. The International Bureau shall provide the secretariat of the various organs of the Union. The Director General shall be the chief executive of the Union and shall represent the Union. The International Bureau shall publish a Gazette and other publications provided for by the Regulations or required by the Assembly. The Director General and any staff member designated by him shall participate, without the right to vote, in all meetings of the Assembly, the Executive Committee and any other committee or working group; the Director General shall be ex officio secretary of these bodies. The International Bureau shall, in accordance with directions of the Assembly and in cooperation with the Executive Committee, make preparations for revision conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IB is secretariat and administrative arm; DG has central executive/representative role and participates in committees without voting rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee for Technical Cooperation objectives and membership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly shall establish a Committee for Technical Cooperation. The Assembly shall determine its composition and appoint its members, with due regard to an equitable representation of developing countries. The International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities shall be ex officio members of the Committee. The aim of the Committee shall be to contribute, by advice and recommendations: (i) to the constant improvement of the services provided for under this Treaty, (ii) to the securing ... of the maximum degree of uniformity in their documentation and working methods and the maximum degree of uniformly high quality in their reports, and (iii) on the initiative of the Assembly or the Executive Committee, to the solution of the technical problems specifically involved in the establishment of a single International Searching Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee includes ISAs/IPEAs ex officio and focuses on service improvement, uniformity, quality and technical problem solving (including potential single ISA establishment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee procedures and transmission of advice
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State and any interested international organization may approach the Committee in writing on questions which fall within the competence of the Committee. The Committee may address its advice and recommendations to the Director General or, through him, to the Assembly, the Executive Committee, all or some of the International Searching and Preliminary Examining Authorities, and all or some of the receiving Offices. The Director General shall transmit to the Executive Committee the texts of all the advice and recommendations of the Committee; he may comment on such texts. The Executive Committee may express its views on any advice, recommendation, or other activity of the Committee, and may invite the Committee to study and report on questions falling within its competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal channels exist for committee input; DG transmits texts to Exec Committee which can comment and request further study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and financing of the Union
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union shall have a budget. The budget shall include the income and expenses proper to the Union and its contribution to the budget of expenses common to the Unions administered by the Organization. Subject to paragraph (5), the budget shall be financed from: (i) fees and charges due for services rendered by the International Bureau in relation to the Union; (ii) sale of, or royalties on, the publications of the International Bureau concerning the Union; (iii) gifts, bequests, and subventions; (iv) rents, interests, and other miscellaneous income. The amounts of fees and charges due to the International Bureau and the prices of its publications shall be so fixed that they should, under normal circumstances, be sufficient to cover all the expenses of the International Bureau connected with the administration of this Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple revenue streams; fee/pricing policy intended to cover IB expenses in normal circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributions to cover deficits and apportionment
rubrics_metrics.description: Should any financial year close with a deficit, the Contracting States shall, subject to provisions, pay contributions to cover such deficit. The amount of the contribution of each Contracting State shall be decided by the Assembly with due regard to the number of international applications which has emanated from each of them in the relevant year. If other means of provisionally covering any deficit are secured, the Assembly may decide that such deficit be carried forward and that the Contracting States should not be asked to pay contributions. If the financial situation permits, the Assembly may decide that any contributions paid be reimbursed to the Contracting States which have paid them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deficit apportionment based on activity (number of international applications); Assembly discretion for provisional coverage or reimbursement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of unpaid contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: A Contracting State which has not paid, within two years of the due date as established by the Assembly, its contribution may not exercise its right to vote in any of the organs of the Union. However, any organ may allow such a State to continue to exercise its right to vote in that organ so long as it is satisfied that the delay in payment is due to exceptional and unavoidable circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-payment for two years can lead to loss of voting rights unless organs permit continued participation for exceptional reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget continuity if not adopted
rubrics_metrics.description: If the budget is not adopted before the beginning of a new financial period, it shall be at the same level as the budget of the previous year, as provided in the financial regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuity measure to avoid operational gaps when a new budget is not adopted in time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working capital fund
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union shall have a working capital fund which shall be constituted by a single payment made by each Contracting State. If the fund becomes insufficient, the Assembly shall arrange to increase it. If part of the fund is no longer needed, it shall be reimbursed. The amount of initial payment or participation in increases shall be decided by the Assembly on the basis of principles similar to those for deficit contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Working capital established by one-time payments; adjustments and reimbursements governed by Assembly decisions and proportionality rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host State advances and ex officio representation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the headquarters agreement with the host State it shall be provided that, whenever the working capital fund is insufficient, such State shall grant advances. As long as it remains under the obligation to grant advances, such State shall have an ex officio seat in the Assembly and on the Executive Committee. The State and the Organization shall each have the right to denounce the obligation to grant advances; denunciation shall take effect three years after the end of the year in which it has been notified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host State may be required to advance funds and receives temporary ex officio seats while under obligation; denunciation has three-year lead time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Auditing of accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The auditing of the accounts shall be effected by one or more of the Contracting States or by external auditors, as provided in the financial regulations. They shall be designated, with their agreement, by the Assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly-designated auditing by State(s) or external auditors according to financial regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations content and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations annexed to this Treaty provide Rules: (i) concerning matters in respect of which this Treaty expressly refers to the Regulations or expressly provides that they are or shall be prescribed, (ii) concerning any administrative requirements, matters, or procedures, (iii) concerning any details useful in the implementation of the provisions of this Treaty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations fill in procedural, administrative and detail-level rules necessary to implement Treaty provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of the Regulations — voting thresholds and special conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Assembly may amend the Regulations. Subject to the provisions of paragraph (3), amendments shall require three-fourths of the votes cast. The Regulations specify the Rules which may be amended (i) only by unanimous consent, or (ii) only if none of the Contracting States whose national Office acts as an International Searching or Preliminary Examining Authority dissents, and, where such Authority is an intergovernmental organization, if the Contracting State member of that organization authorized for that purpose by the other member States within the competent body of such organization does not dissent. Exclusion or inclusion of such Rules requires fulfillment of the respective conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some Regulations are subject to enhanced consensus requirements (unanimity or no dissent by relevant national Offices/States) for amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision of the Treaty
rubrics_metrics.description: This Treaty may be revised from time to time by a special conference of the Contracting States. The convocation of any revision conference shall be decided by the Assembly. Any intergovernmental organization appointed as International Searching or Preliminary Examining Authority shall be admitted as observer to any revision conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision requires a special conference convened by the Assembly; ISAs/IPEAs (intergovernmental) may observe.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute settlement between Contracting States
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 64(5), any dispute between two or more Contracting States concerning the interpretation or application of this Treaty or the Regulations, not settled by negotiation, may, by any one of the States concerned, be brought before the International Court of Justice by application in conformity with the Statute of the Court, unless the States concerned agree on some other method of settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ICJ is default forum for interstate disputes over Treaty interpretation/application unless parties agree otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment procedure for certain specified Articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals for the amendment of Articles 53(5), (9) and (11), 54, 55(4) to (8), 56, and 57 may be initiated by any State member of the Assembly, by the Executive Committee, or by the Director General. Such proposals shall be communicated by the Director General to the Contracting States at least six months in advance of their consideration by the Assembly. Amendments to the Articles referred to shall be adopted by the Assembly; adoption shall require three-fourths of the votes cast. Any amendment shall enter into force one month after written notifications of acceptance have been received by the Director General from three-fourths of the States members of the Assembly at the time it adopted the amendment. An amendment increasing financial obligations shall bind only those States which have notified their acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special advance notice, supermajority adoption and multi-State notification thresholds apply; financial-obligation-increasing amendments bind only consenting States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Becoming party to the Treaty (accession and ratification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State member of the International Union for the Protection of Industrial Property may become party to this Treaty by: (i) signature followed by the deposit of an instrument of ratification, or (ii) deposit of an instrument of accession. Instruments of ratification or accession shall be deposited with the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership channel limited to States that are members of the International Union; deposit with DG required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry into force conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to provisions, this Treaty shall enter into force three months after eight States have deposited their instruments of ratification or accession, provided that at least four of those States each fulfill any of the following conditions: (i) the number of applications filed in the State has exceeded 40,000 according to the most recent annual statistics; (ii) the nationals or residents of the State have filed at least 1,000 applications in one foreign country according to the most recent annual statistics; (iii) the national Office of the State has received at least 10,000 applications from nationals or residents of foreign countries according to the most recent annual statistics. For these purposes 'applications' does not include utility models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry into force requires not just 8 instruments but also activity thresholds met by at least 4 of those States to ensure initial operational capacity and participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of Chapter II and its conditional activation
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of Chapter II and the corresponding provisions of the Regulations shall become applicable only on the date on which three States each of which fulfill at least one of the three requirements specified in paragraph (1) have become party to this Treaty without declaring that they do not intend to be bound by the provisions of Chapter II. That date shall not be prior to that of the initial entry into force under paragraph (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter II (substantive international filing/processing provisions) comes into effect only when a minimum set of active States accept to be bound.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reservations and special declarations by States
rubrics_metrics.description: Any State may declare that it shall not be bound by the provisions of Chapter II. States may also make declarations that they shall not be bound by Article 39(1) with respect to furnishing a copy and translation, that the obligation to delay national processing shall not prevent publication by its national Office, or that international publication is not required for them. States may declare that filing outside the State is not equated to an actual filing in that State for prior art purposes, with concomitant statements of the date and conditions of prior art effect. Declarations must be made in writing and take effect six months after receipt by the Director General; withdrawals take effect three months after receipt. No reservations other than those specified are permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple types of permitted declarations with defined notice and effect periods; expresses strict limits on allowed reservations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradual application when an Authority has transitional processing limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agreement with any International Searching or Preliminary Examining Authority provides, transitionally, for limits on the number or kind of international applications that such Authority undertakes to process, the Assembly shall adopt the measures necessary for the gradual application of this Treaty and the Regulations in respect of given categories of international applications. This provision shall also apply to requests for an international-type search under Article 15(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assembly must manage phased implementation where Authorities have transitional processing limitations; Assembly also fixes dates from which applications and demands may be filed, not later than six months after Treaty entry into force or Chapter II application date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denunciation procedure and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any Contracting State may denounce this Treaty by notification addressed to the Director General. Denunciation shall take effect six months after receipt of the said notification by the Director General. It shall not affect the effects of the international application in the denouncing State if the international application was filed, and, where the denouncing State has been elected, the election was made, prior to the expiration of the said six-month period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denunciation is effected by written notification and has a six-month delay; prior-filed international applications remain effective in the denouncing State if filed/elected before expiry of the period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature, certified copies and languages
rubrics_metrics.description: This Treaty shall be signed in a single original in the English and French languages, both texts being equally authentic. The Director General shall transmit two copies, certified by him, of this Treaty and the Regulations annexed hereto to the Governments of all States party to the Paris Convention and, on request, to any other State. Official texts shall be established by the Director General, after consultation with interested Governments, in the German, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish languages, and such other languages as the Assembly may designate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English and French are equally authentic; DG provides certified copies and may establish other official language texts after consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director General depositary and registration functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The original of this Treaty, when no longer open for signature, shall be deposited with the Director General. The Director General shall transmit certified copies of the Treaty and Regulations, and shall register this Treaty with the Secretariat of the United Nations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG acts as depositary and is responsible for transmission and UN registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications to Contracting States by Director General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director General shall notify the Governments of all States party to the Paris Convention of: (i) signatures under Article 62, (ii) deposits of instruments of ratification or accession under Article 62, (iii) the date of entry into force of this Treaty and the date from which Chapter II is applicable, (iv) any declarations made under Article 64(1) to (5), (v) withdrawals of any declarations made under Article 64(6)(b), (vi) denunciations received under Article 66, (vii) any declarations made under Article 31(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DG is charged with formal notification duties to ensure transparency of status changes and declarations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulations — detailed formal requirements for international applications (Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations (Table of Contents) include Rules on: The Request (Form and Contents); The Description; The Claims; The Drawings; The Abstract; Expressions, etc., not to be used; Terminology and Signs; Physical Requirements of the International Application; Language of the International Application and Translations for the Purposes of International Search and International Publication; Submission by the Applicant of Documents Relating to Earlier Search; Unity of Invention; Inventions Relating to Biological Material; Nucleotide and/or Amino Acid Sequence Listings; The Transmittal Fee; The International Filing Fee; The Search Fee; Extension of Time Limits for Payment of Fees; The Priority Document; The Applicant; The Competent Receiving Office; International Filing Date; Preparation of Copies; Transmittal of the Record Copy and Translation; Transmittal of the Search Copy, Translation and Sequence Listing; Receipt of the Record Copy by the International Bureau; Receipt of the Search Copy by the International Searching Authority; Checking by, and Correcting before, the Receiving Office of Certain Elements of the International Application; Correction or Addition of Priority Claim; Correction or Addition of Declarations, Indications, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulations provide comprehensive procedural and form requirements for international applications (see enumerated Rule headings). The Table of Contents itself signals the breadth of formal and content requirements applicants and Offices must follow.
